records.location: sheet 'Financial Contribution (Y)' cell G100 (row 100 col G)
records.note: Fines and penalties at Haile; cell comment: fine paid for exceeding permit discharge limits of total cadmium, free cyanide and chronic effluent toxicity in events in 2020 and 2021.

observations: No volume units anywhere (Unit column just says "Actual"). Withdrawal/discharge inferred as ML and consumption as m3 because 2021 and 2022 total consumption (6,838,696 / 8,849,299) equal withdrawal minus discharge in ML x1000 (33,106 - 26,267 = 6,839; 35,650 - 26,801 = 8,849). Consumption values were divided by 1,000.

Methodology break in 2021: water harvested now includes rainwater (cell comments G62-G66; Didipio/Waihi add rainwater temporarily stored then discharged, Haile uses change-in-storage, Macraes a rational-method calculation). Consumption flipped from negative (2018-2020: -6,200 / -2,546 / -5,654 ML) to positive (2021: +6,839; 2022: +8,849 ML) and total withdrawal jumped from 21,734 ML (2020 legacy block) to 33,106 ML (2021). The series are not comparable across 2020/2021.
2022 quality reporting switched from TDS-based Freshwater/Other (2021) to MCA WAF Categories 1-3 (cell comments on H74 etc.), so 2021 and 2022 quality splits are not comparable.

Internal inconsistency 2021 "All areas" surface water: freshwater 1,207 / other 14,358 (G136-G137), but the site rows sum the other way round (freshwater 704+9,176+2,412+2,066 = 14,358; other 0+0+1,188+19 = 1,207). The all-areas split appears swapped. 2022 all-areas ground water total (H141) is blank.

Haile: 2021 third-party take could not be quantified (council data recording error, comment G132; 0 reported, meter installed); no "Total water discharge" row for Haile, so all-areas 2021 total 26,267 vs surface 26,268 (rounding). 2021 Haile fine US$12,600 (and 2022 US$22,172; 2020 US$111,200, nature not stated) - the 2021 fine was for exceeding permit discharge limits for cadmium, free cyanide and chronic effluent toxicity in 2020-2021 events.

Legacy 2018-2020 block: 2018 site-level cells (16 cells) are all 0 while the all-operations 2018 values are non-zero (e.g. surface discharge 28,204), so the site zeros were treated as placeholders and not extracted. 2018 "Total volume discharged" (22,004) equals 2018 withdrawn exactly - likely a copy error. The FY18 column also shows 0 placeholders for other metrics (e.g. renewable shares, TSF counts).

Didipio dominates: 22,592 / 21,239 ML withdrawn in 2021/2022 (68% / 60% of group), 21,062 / 21,758 ML discharged; 2022 includes 5,759 ML Category 3 groundwater. Didipio direct energy collapsed in 2020 (8,551 GJ vs 144,400 GJ in 2019, consistent with its operational suspension), yet its legacy-block 2020 groundwater take is still 14,897 ML and surface discharge 22,577 ML.

OceanaGold reports 0% of operations in areas of water stress for 2018-2022 and 0 withdrawal/discharge in stressed areas. Moderate-to-major environmental spills: 0 at all sites all years. Minor environmental non-compliances fell 51 (2018) -> 19 (2022), mostly Macraes.
Workbook period-end/reported dates: FY18 column carries a reported date of 05-04-2023, i.e. was (re)populated later; values for 2018 should be treated with caution.
